examples.note: Recursive binary search; the upper-half recursive call is `binsearch(mid, end)` instead of `binsearch(mid + 1, end)`, an off-by-one boundary bug.

levels.reference: Mutation testing boundary/statement operators (Offutt et al.) - e.g. off-by-one boundary conditions; QuixBugs benchmark (Lin & Koppel) for real single-line Python defect examples in this family.

examples.note: Kernighan's bit-count trick uses `n ^= n - 1` instead of `n &= n - 1` - a wrong bitwise operator (XOR swapped for AND) that produces an incorrect count on the main path, not just an edge case.

levels.reference: Mutation testing operators (Offutt et al.): ROR (Relational Operator Replacement - wrong comparison operator), COR (Conditional Operator Replacement - inverted/wrong boolean logic), AOR (Arithmetic Operator Replacement). QuixBugs benchmark for real examples.
MITRE CWE (Common Weakness Enumeration): CWE-89 (SQL injection), CWE-306 (missing authentication for a critical function), CWE-287 (improper authentication), CWE-798 (use of hardcoded credentials).
CWE-1069 (Empty Exception Block), CWE-703 (Improper Check or Handling of Exceptional Conditions). Codified in static-analysis rules: Bandit B110 (try_except_pass), CodeQL 'empty except' query.
Classic code-smell catalog (Fowler, Refactoring): Duplicated Code, Dead Code, leftover-comment/debug-print smells. Not a numbered standard like CWE - a canonical but informal practitioner reference.

Community-documented Python gotchas (Hitchhiker's Guide to Python 'Common Gotchas', Real Python) - e.g. mutable default arguments. Informal community consensus, not a formal taxonomy; treat definitions here as lower-confidence than the CWE/mutation-testing-grounded flavors.
